subject: sperm whale
title: The 5 Biggest Brains on Earth, Ranked (Yours Is Only #5)

scenes.text: The five biggest brains on the planet, by weight. Yours scrapes in at number five.

scenes.label: Human · 1.4 kg
scenes.text: Number five: you. A human brain weighs about 1.3 to 1.4 kilograms. Big for your body size, small for this list.

scenes.label: Bottlenose dolphin · 1.6 kg
scenes.text: Number four: the bottlenose dolphin, 1.5 to 1.7 kilograms. Slightly bigger than yours, inside a body about the same weight.

scenes.label: Elephant · 5 kg
scenes.text: Number three: the elephant, around 5 kilograms. The heaviest brain of any land animal, about four times a human's.

scenes.label: Orca · up to 6.8 kg
scenes.text: Number two: the orca, 5.4 to 6.8 kilograms. Big enough to run hunts that take a whole pod working as one.

scenes.label: Sperm whale · 7.8 kg
scenes.text: Number one: the sperm whale. 7.8 kilograms on average in a grown male, the biggest brain of any animal ever known. Nearly six times yours.

description:
The five biggest brains on Earth, ranked by mass. A mature male sperm whale's brain averages 7.8 kilograms, the largest known brain of any animal; orcas come next at 5.4 to 6.8 kilograms, then elephants at about 5 kilograms.
Bottlenose dolphins, at 1.5 to 1.7 kilograms, edge out the human brain's 1.3 to 1.4 kilograms.
Does a bigger brain mean a smarter animal?
first_comment: Bonus: the long-finned pilot whale has more neurons in its neocortex than any mammal tested, humans included. Which would you put at number one, and what should we rank next?
